A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PSSC/Adaptive Scope research. Their text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original node-classification experiments, optimal-scope analyses, component ablations and embedding visualizations in Tables 1–4 and Figures 1–4.

after.justification: v2 reports original benchmark results, revised ablations and training-time measurements, alongside retained scope and embedding analyses.

M1.justification: v1 combines structural encodings, node features and concatenated GNN logits through concatenation-based fusion. v2 adds graph propagation of those logits into multi-hop label embeddings and introduces attention-based fusion alongside concatenation (Sections 5.2–5.3 and Appendix C). These substantially change AS inputs and architecture; the depth-selection framework, loss and train-validation resplitting remain.

E1.justification: Across the complete PDFs, the same nine datasets and graph node-classification tasks remain represented. Flickr disappears from Table 1 but remains in Figure 2. Changes to which retained datasets appear in particular comparisons and ablations do not introduce a new task, population or domain.

E2.justification: v2 Table 4 adds standalone SGC and GAT comparators beside the AS ablations; v1 Table 4 contains only full and ablated AS variants. The main benchmark baseline families and Table 2 leaderboard comparators remain. GCNII and ACM-GCN were already evaluated in v1.

E3.justification: v2 Table 3 introduces runtime evaluation with six-layer timing references, AS-only training costs and a 256-unit AS width cap. Table 4 changes the ablation reference from all inputs to the best tuned input configuration, and Table 1 excludes nonconverged ACM-GCN/genius from average improvement. Penn94's reported edge count also changes from 449,878 to 1.3M without explaining whether the graph changed.

E4.justification: Table 4 replaces the original feature/logit ablations with checks on the revised label embeddings, removes the separate raw-feature ablation and extends the component study to Squirrel. Appendix E adds qualitative sensitivity findings for smoothing depth, fusion choice and width. The depth curves and t-SNE analysis are retained; t-SNE is only relocated.

E5.justification: Both versions specify ten runs per benchmark and use the same plus/minus reporting practice in their result tables. No new seed information, uncertainty estimator, confidence interval or significance test is introduced.

E6.justification: Table 1 adds broad GCNII-AS and ACM-GCN-AS results, updates many existing scores and removes Flickr entries. Reported SGC-AS/Penn94 accuracy changes from 82.40 to 83.84, while ACM-GCN/genius ROC-AUC changes from 80.33 to 64.74, flagged as nonconvergence in v2. Table 2 updates GCNII-AS/PubMed from 91.66 to 91.88; runtime and revised ablation results are also added. Method and setting changes prevent interpreting these as controlled same-setting gains.

T1.justification: The CSBM assumptions, Theorem 1 and Appendix A proof are retained, apart from numbering and notation. A limited formal change is the revised predictor complexity bound: v2 Section 5.3 omits the raw-feature-dimension term present in v1 Section 5.1.

C1.justification: The introduction changes its performance contribution from up to 4.27% average improvement across nine datasets to 2.70–6.04% for five architectures across eight main benchmarks. The central claims about PSSC novelty, mitigating overfitting, architectural flexibility and leading performance remain.

C2.justification: v1 explains GAT's larger gains through expressivity and overfitting; v2 instead contrasts GCNII's similar representations across depths with ACM-GCN's diversity and overfitting. Appendix E adds applicability qualifications for input features and label smoothing, including noisy 4–6-hop pseudo-labels on arxiv-year. The central interpretation of depth-dependent generalization remains.

D1.justification: v1 mainly provides search ranges and general implementation settings. v2 Appendix E and Table 7 disclose dataset-by-model choices for depth, validation ratio, masking, inputs, smoothing, fusion and MLP hyperparameters. Appendix C specifies both fusion implementations, while runtime accounting and the snap-patents memory-related width limit are documented. This substantially expands reproducibility information.

R1.justification: v2 removes the GraphMoE discussion and reference, plus Gao et al.'s node-adaptive propagation reference. It adds explicit connections between its fusion implementations and previously cited mixing methods. Most research positioning and cited works remain unchanged after matching renumbered references.

P1.justification: Editing concentrates on method explanations, experimental interpretation and hyperparameter guidance. Method subsections are reorganized, Section 6.5 moves to Appendix D, and appendices are reordered. Duplicated related-work prose and the placeholder acknowledgment are removed; most introductory and theoretical text and the conclusion remain.

P2.justification: Several evidence displays are substantially redesigned: Table 1 expands paired base/AS rows, Table 3 becomes a full-width accuracy/runtime comparison, and Table 4 replaces score differences with absolute results and baseline rows. A large configuration table is added as Table 7. Figure 4 moves to the appendix, and Figure 2 gains SOTA reference lines and a fuller caption.

improvement.justification: v2 improves reproducibility through explicit fusion implementations and detailed AS configurations, and adds useful evidence on architectural generality and incremental training cost. These gains are qualified by reduced main-table reporting for Flickr and inconsistencies such as Section 6.1 claiming ten benchmarks while Table 1 contains eight. The runtime comparison excludes base-GNN training, so it supports only incremental costs. The net quality improvement is positive but limited.
